Donald Trump was seen with a mega-glass of Diet Coke at the White House Correspondents' Dinner

President Donald Trump's love for Diet Coke was well documented during his first term, but Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has negative views of the president's eating habits.

On Friday night, Trump was spotted with a massive glass of Diet Coke at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, seemingly disregarding his health secretary's advice. As the president prepares to deliver remarks for take two of the black-tie event, he was seen enjoying his favorite drink.

It comes as Health and Human Services Secretary RFK Jr. claimed Trump has the most "unhinged" eating habits. "He eats really bad food, which is McDonald's and candy and Diet Coke," Kennedy Jr. said on Katie Miller's podcast. "He drinks Diet Coke at all times; he has the constitution of a deity. I don't know how he's alive."

Trump told the secretary that he only eats junk food when he's traveling, but when he's at Mar-a-Lago or at the White House, "he's eating really good food." Kennedy Jr. said that if a person travels with Trump, they're under the belief that he's "pumping himself full of poison all day long."

A clip of Kennedy Jr. remarks went viral online, with one person calling it the "only factual point" he's ever made. Another person wrote: "Trump is not only poisoning himself with what he puts in his mouth, but he also spews poison throughout the U.S. and the world every time he opens his mouth."

Earlier this year, Trump raised eyebrows over comments he made that diet soda could prevent cancer, according to Dr. Mehmet OZ, the administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. Oz made the claim during an interview with Donald Trump Jr. in an April episode of the latter's podcast, Triggered with Don Jr.

"Your dad argues that diet soda is good for him because it kills grass—if poured on grass—so, therefore, it must kill cancer cells inside the body," said Oz.

Trump drinks a Diet Coke during the ProAm of the LIV Golf Team Championship at Trump National Doral Golf Club in October 2022(Image: AP)

"You know, we were on Air Force One the other day, and I walk in there because he wants to talk about something, and he's got an orange soft drink on his desk. He's got a Fanta on the desk, and I say, ‘Are you kidding me?’ So he starts to, like, sheepishly grin. He says, ‘You know, this stuff’s good for me, it kills cancer cells.’"

Oz, a former cardiothoracic surgeon, also claimed that Trump once joked with him that Fanta couldn't be that unhealthy for him because it's "fresh-squeezed." Trump Jr. tried to defend his father, suggesting, "maybe he's onto something."
